subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Acme)

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard + proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Pain points you shared:
- Vendor lock-in and rising costs on current OpenAI/Anthropic consumption (especially embeddings spikes when reindexing).
- Latency variability and occasional timeouts on peak queries (customer-facing chat).
- Compliance requirements: KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2 evidence, and SSO for internal tooling.
- Need to run a consistent eval suite to avoid quality regressions during any migration.

Current stack (as stated):
- Generation: OpenAI (chat/completions) + Anthropic (safety checks) for a subset of flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for semantic search and vector DB indexing.
- Orchestration: internal API wrapper that expects OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function-calling.
- Infra: production traffic ~40-60 rps peak, Azure hosting, prefer dedicated GPU pool for predictable throughput.

Success criteria for a migration POC:
- Maintain or improve perceived generation quality on the agreed eval set (>=95% pass on key prompts).
- Reduce per-token/embedding unit cost by ~30-40% (measured on baseline workload).
- Compatible API surface (streaming + function-call support + embeddings) with minimal code changes (< 2 engineer-weeks).
- Meet security/compliance checklist: KMS + audit logs + SOC2 artifact access.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 600ms, p95 < 2s for typical chat requests.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial recommendation):
- Llama 2 family (7B / 13B) - good accuracy / low-latency when quantized (q4).
- Mistral-instruct variants (7B) - strong instruction-following with cost-efficiency.
- Falcon-40B / 180B instruct candidates - if you want higher-capability fallbacks for specific prompts.
- Hosted vs Private options: we can run any of the above on Redwood Hosted (fast onboarding) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem for stricter controls).

Immediate next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive: schedule a session with your platform engineers + our infra/solutions team to review integration points (streaming, function-calls, KV cache, quantization).
2) Share security questionnaire + baseline eval prompts (we attached preliminary questionnaire + product deck).
3) Redwood to propose a 2-4 week pilot plan and cost estimate with a recommended model + quantization profile.

Proposed meeting times next week for the deep-dive - are you available Wed 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 9:00-10:00 PT?

Attachments: security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx, redwood-product-deck.pdf

Thanks - looking forward to moving quickly.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa, great summary, this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Primary production use case is customer support chat + internal semantic search (embeddings for a ~30M document index).
- Current production traffic is ~50 rps peak; embeddings are run both at ingest and periodic full reindexes which cause cost spikes.
- We need the ability to run in our Azure tenancy (preferred) with dedicated GPU pools and KMS for key management. SOC2 + SSO (Okta) are must-haves for any pilot.

I'll loop in our platform lead (cc'd) for the deep-dive - they'd like to see an integration plan that minimizes code changes (we have an internal OpenAI-compatible wrapper).

Availability: Wed 10:00-11:00 PT works for our team. Please send a calendar invite and include any pre-read (security checklist + eval prompts).

Attaching current-costs.csv that shows monthly consumption by endpoint - this should help with the cost model in the pilot proposal.

Regards,
Olivia Chen
Head of Product Operations | Acme Commerce
olivia.chen@acme.com
Attachments: current-costs.csv
